title: story-032 removed the precondition that made 'fund the streamer before wiring the minter' impossible (deployment-ordering footgun)
description: Before 9611312, isNudgeToken(token) == true TRANSITIVELY WITNESSED tokenMinter != 0 && dispatcherIndex != 0 && dispatcher != 0, because no whitelist entry could be added without _resolvePaymentPath() succeeding. registerStream gates on nothing else. story-032 removed that gate. Now: whitelist -> register -> PERMISSIONLESS collectNudge funds the buffer (production NudgeRatchet does it on schedule) -> batchMint reverts BatchMint__MinterNotConfigured at :479 BEFORE the flush loop -> nothing drains it, and the streamer has no rescue.
impact: Donor funds accumulate in a streamer buffer that nothing can drain until minter configuration is completed. Fully recoverable by completing configuration => RUNBOOK HAZARD, not a loss.
magnitude: ECON-26-M2: both production donors are STATELESS SWEEPERS forwarding their ENTIRE balance on every dispatch, so the amount at risk is ALL DONOR THROUGHPUT between registerStream and completed minter configuration - not a fixed sum.
shippedDocumentationAssertsTheHazardAway: *** ADDED 2026-07-30 (remediation pass) - THE CITATION THIS RECORD PREVIOUSLY OMITTED, AND THE STRONGEST FORM OF THE LAW-3 TEST. *** src/BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol:317-320, added by the SAME commit that removed the gate, reads VERBATIM: '/// Because nothing here reads the payment path, adding works while /// `tokenMinter`/`dispatcherIndex` are unset - symmetric with /// removal, AND NO LONGER AN ORDERING CONSTRAINT ON DEPLOYMENT /// SCRIPTS.' AN ORDERING CONSTRAINT DOES REMAIN (whitelist -> registerStream -> permissionless collectNudge from a stateless sweeping donor -> batchMint reverts BatchMint__MinterNotConfigured at :479 BEFORE the flush loop -> nothing drains the buffer, and the streamer has no rescue). SO: an operator who strands donor throughput here is NOT BEING RECKLESS - THEY ARE FOLLOWING A LINE OF SHIPPED DOCUMENTATION THAT TELLS THEM THE CONSTRAINT WAS LIFTED. The hazard is not merely non-obvious, it is AFFIRMATIVELY CONTRADICTED BY THE PROJECT'S OWN DOCUMENTATION - the class the standing rule says RAISES rather than lowers severity. This converts the finding from 'the hazard is undisclosed' to 'the hazard is affirmatively denied', places it unambiguously in scope, and FORECLOSES any later attempt to re-triage it as an admin mistake. It also makes L-04 and F-02-032 A MATCHED PAIR: the same false conclusion in the story ('NudgeStreamer ... is unaffected') and in the source. NOTE ON THE CITATION: the severity audit cited this as ':318-320'; the quoted sentence begins at :317 - use :317-320.
severityNote: Low - CONFIRMED by the independent severity audit, on the argument this record previously UNDER-USED. THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT FOR LOW: IN THE PARKED STATE batchMint REVERTS FOR EVERYONE. The contract is not mis-sequenced-but-working, it is entirely non-functional - so this is a BRING-UP WINDOW in which nobody is minting and the condition ANNOUNCES ITSELF ON THE FIRST SMOKE TEST. Value parking during pre-commission, in protocol custody, in a state that is LOUD and UNILATERALLY UNLOCKABLE by the owner (setTokenMinter + setDispatcherIndex), is Low. Both escalation branches were taken and both fail: (1) 'configuration is never completed' is the ABSENCE OF A DEPLOYMENT, not an attack path and not a C4 protocol-function impact, with the unilateral unlock available throughout; (2) 'the batchMinter is repointed' is PERMANENT stranding (the buffer is keyed (batchMinter, token) and only that msg.sender can pullPendingStream) but is ALREADY TRACKED at Low as 4a1d8edc92, whose title covers both the decommission and the permanent-de-whitelist case. The COMPOUND of the two (new route in + no way out) was considered for Medium and DECLINED AFFIRMATIVELY: it needs two privileged actions and strands only optional-incentive funds already sunk from yield (opportunity cost, not loss), and the compounding is recorded rather than hidden. Deployment-ordering footgun (Law 3: non-obvious, indeed affirmatively denied => in scope), fully recoverable, no loss.
recommendation: PREFERRED - ONE CHANGE CLOSES THREE OPEN ITEMS: add a rescueERC20-equivalent, or better a deregisterStream, to NudgeStreamer. That single change closes L-04, ledger 4a1d8edc92 ('the streamer has no rescue', open) AND the permanent-de-whitelist stranding at once - three open items, one fix, which is more useful to the owner than three separate documentation asks. This should be stated as the PREFERRED mitigation, not only the ordering-precondition restore. Honour the standing counter-argument recorded against 4a1d8edc92 (an owner rescue would let the owner divert third-party donations, and the pass-through-no-custody design is defensible): a deregisterStream that settles to the REGISTERED BATCHMINTER rather than to an owner-chosen address satisfies both concerns. ALSO, AND INDEPENDENTLY: restore a config-completeness precondition on setNudgeTokenWhitelist (or add one to NudgeStreamer.registerStream); AND CORRECT THE NATSPEC AT :317-320 - as written it is the affirmative misstatement quoted in shippedDocumentationAssertsTheHazardAway, and leaving it while adding a runbook note elsewhere would leave the misstatement to win. Document the required ordering explicitly: complete minter configuration BEFORE whitelisting and registering a stream. Fold the remediation into story-032 while it is still open (see F-05-032).
